issues.legal_issue: A court-ordered stay of a process of executing a decree, even when partial, permits the period of the stay to be excluded when computing the limitation period for execution.
material_facts: A decree was being executed against judgment-debtors and a surety, whose properties had been attached.
While an appeal concerning the attachment was pending, a judicial order kept the properties attached but stayed further proceedings for their sale.
After the stay was dissolved, a later execution application was challenged as having been filed beyond the prescribed limitation period.
issues.conclusion: The period during which the sale process was stayed was excludable when computing the limitation period for execution; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15(1) of the Limitation Act, 1908 controlled the limitation rule in section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. “Execution” in section 15(1) includes all appropriate means of enforcing a decree and processes or proceedings in aid of, or supplemental to, execution. A stay of any execution process is a stay of execution, regardless of the stage, property, or judgment-debtor concerned. The Court agreed with the broad approach in Sreenath Roy v. Radhanath Mookerjee and approved Bai Ujam v. Bai Ruxmani, Govindnath Chaudhuri v. Basiruddin Mondal, and Sitaram v. Chunnilalsa. It rejected the contrary approaches in Kundo Mal v. Firm Daulat Ram Vidya Prakash, Virchand Kapur Chand v. Marualappa, and Chanbasappa v. Holibasappa, and explained that Kirtyanand Singh v. Prithi Chand Lal did not establish a contrary rule.

predicates.execution_limitation_proceeding: The matter concerns a proceeding to execute a decree that is subject to a limitation period.
predicates.court_order_stayed_execution_process: A court order prevented the decree-holder from pursuing a process used to enforce the decree.

issues.definition: When an execution proceeding is subject to a limitation period and a court order stays an execution process, the period of that stay is excluded from the limitation computation.
